rename.to: 文件缓存反序列化失败

body: I have the same error. It seems to be dependent on high-load. I'll provide more details as soon as I will find cache files and its contents..

I found a topic on forum: http://www.yiiframework.com/forum/index.php/topic/62729-php-notice-yiibaseerrorexception-with-message-unserialize-error-at-offset-0-of-14838-bytes/
And issue in this repository: https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/issues/4820

But file locking is already applied:
\yii\caching\FileCache:131

```
        if (@file_put_contents($cacheFile, $value, LOCK_EX) !== false) {
```
Hmm... what's the file system? Does it support exclusive locks?
@samdark ext3, of course it supports exclusive locks.
Yes. It would be useful to test this thing alone and see what happens...

@iworker https://secure.php.net/manual/en/function.flock.php#refsect1-function.flock-notes:

> On Linux, the file system will also need to be mounted with the mand option for this to work.

@samdark It doesn't help.
I checked filesystem with mount and it was actually been mounted without mand option.
I remounted it with mand option:

```
mount | grep /home
/dev/md2 on /home type ext4 (rw,relatime,mand,discard,data=ordered)
```

After that I ran my script:

```
seq 1 32 | xargs -L1 -P16  ./yii test/cache
```

And finally I got:

```
++++++++++++++++++Error: unserialize(): Error at offset 5218303 of 5218304 bytes
Error: unserialize(): Error at offset 5218303 of 5218304 bytes
Error: unserialize(): Error at offset 5218303 of 5218304 bytes
Error: unserialize(): Error at offset 5218303 of 5218304 bytes
Error: unserialize(): Error at offset 5218303 of 5218304 bytes
Error: unserialize(): Error at offset 5218303 of 5218304 bytes
++++++++++++++
```

So, problem is not with mand.

@samdark Maybe it would be a good solution to rewrite cache reading/writing using fopen/flock/fclose?
At least reading. If it will use flock() when reading, probably it will solve a problem.
